statements.t: • our ability to realize the expected benefits from our cash-generating and cost savings initiatives in our United States ("U.S.") business;
• our ability to execute our long-term (PRA 3.0) strategy effectively, including the targets related to improving our financial results;
• Maintenance of a diversified capital structure, consistent with our targeted leverage and liquidity objectives.
In Europe, portfolio supply continued to trend higher, and we expect that trend will continue into the fourth quarter.
Our focus continues to be on net returns, which considers the amount and timing of the projected cash collections, estimated costs to collect, funding costs, risk and agreement terms.

Our total portfolio revenue in Q3 2026 decreased by $24.8 million, or 8.0%, compared to Q3 2025, driven by lower Changes in expected recoveries, which decreased by $37.1 million, partially offset by higher Portfolio income, which increased by $12.2 million.

The decrease in Changes in expected recoveries reflected lower recoveries collected in excess of forecast and lower changes in expected future recoveries following the June 30, 2026 update to the forecasts for the majority of our European pools, which reflected sustained cash collections overperformance across multiple markets, among other factors.
Portfolio income, the yield component of our revenue, which is more predictable than Changes in expected recoveries, increased by 4.7% for the quarter and 7.7% year-to-date.
Overperformance in Europe moderated following the update to the forecasts for the majority of our European pools as of June 30, 2026.

The increase reflects purchases of government securities and corporate notes by our banking subsidiary, AK Nordic AB, which is part of our European operations and is expected to continue to operate with similarly higher levels of liquidity moving forward.
• "Estimated remaining collections" or "ERC" refers to the sum of all future projected cash collections on our nonperforming loan portfolios.
• "Finance receivables" or "receivables" refers to the negative allowance for expected recoveries recorded on our balance sheet as an asset.
• "Negative allowance" refers to the present value of cash flows expected to be collected on our finance receivables.
